title: Simple Extensions of Single-Objective Acquisition Functions and Hedge Strategies for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
claim: Simple extensions of standard acquisition functions match or beat specialized multi-objective baselines across diverse benchmarks, reaching lower regret faster.
layout: 3x3 grid of line plots, shared legend and axis labels at bottom
description: A 3x3 grid of line plots, one per synthetic or real-world multi-objective benchmark: ZDT2, ZDT4, ZDT6, DTLZ1, DTLZ2, DTLZ3, Branin Currin, Welded Beam and Vehicle Crash. Each panel title gives the problem dimension and number of objectives. The y-axis is log-normalized hypervolume gap, shared in label across panels, and every curve starts at 0 and falls over 25 epochs after initial sampling. Eight methods appear as colored lines with translucent shaded standard-deviation bands: qHAX-UCB in red, qHAX-EI in blue, MO-Hedge 1 in purple, MO-Hedge 2 in orange, qMOJES in yellow, qHVKG in brown, qLNParEGO in pink and qLNEHVI in gray. One legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the red and orange curves, which usually sit lowest.
caption: Log-normalized hypervolume gap for batch optimization (\(Q=3\)) across synthetic benchmarks. Lower values are better. Mean (solid line) \(\pm 1\) standard deviation (shaded) over 20 runs.
abstract: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) is commonly approached through specialized acquisition functions or scalarization schemes designed to explicitly account for trade-offs among non-preferential objectives. In this work, we show that such complexity might be unnecessary. We propose a framework that extends standard single-objective acquisition functions directly to the multi-objective setting through a hypervolume-based methodology. We further extend hedge strategies for acquisition functions, which are typically used only in single-objective optimization, to the multi-objective regime. Our approach requires minimal modification to existing Bayesian optimization pipelines and avoids the need for bespoke multi-objective formulations. We demonstrate how a broad class of commonly used single-objective acquisition functions and hedge strategies can be adapted in a principled manner to handle multiple objectives, while preserving their intuitive interpretation and computational efficiency. Empirically, we evaluate the proposed methods across a range of synthetic and real-world multi-objective benchmarks. Despite their simplicity, our extensions consistently match or outperform more complex state-of-the-art MOBO methods in terms of optimization performance and sample efficiency. These results suggest that effective multi-objective Bayesian optimization can be achieved by reusing and carefully extending well-established single-objective acquisition strategies, offering a simpler and more flexible alternative to existing approaches.
